entries.title: Annual roof inspection
entries.description: Inspect for damage, wear, and potential leaks.

entries.title: Check for damaged shingles
entries.description: Roofer walks the roof looking for missing, curled, or cracked shingles. Part of the annual inspection or a dedicated post-storm visit.
entries.notes: Also after major storms

entries.title: Reseal flashing and seams
entries.description: Roofer inspects every flashing detail (chimney, vent stacks, parapet walls, equipment curbs) and re-applies sealant where the original membrane has lifted, cracked, or pulled away. Pays particular attention to scuppers and drains where ponding water finds the smallest gap. Critical on flat / membrane roofs because gravity isn't helping you here.
entries.notes: Schedule before the spring rains. A skipped year can mean a leak path that isn't visible from inside until it's done $5K+ of damage to the ceiling and contents below.

entries.title: Treat moss and algae
entries.description: Roofer applies a zinc-strip or oxygen-bleach moss/algae treatment to prevent the dark streaks and shingle damage that biological growth causes. The streaks aren't just cosmetic — moss lifts the granular surface of asphalt shingles and shortens the roof's life by 5–10 years if left untreated.
entries.notes: Wood shake roofs are fragile and slippery — always pro-only with safety gear. For asphalt, fall application means the rains carry the treatment evenly across the shingles before winter. North-facing slopes show moss first; check those when deciding if you're due.

entries.description: Apply asphalt sealer to protect the driveway against UV, water, and oil damage. Extends driveway life significantly over unsealed asphalt.
entries.notes: Early fall while daytime temps are still warm enough for the sealer to cure. About 3 hours DIY for a typical driveway, or book an asphalt service for a no-effort finish.

entries.title: HVAC tune-up (cooling)
entries.description: HVAC tech inspects and services the air conditioning system before summer. Includes refrigerant level check, condenser coil cleaning, capacitor and contactor inspection, blower motor lubrication, condensate drain flush, and a full system performance test under load. Catches small issues before they become a hot-day breakdown.
entries.notes: Book in February or early March. Most HVAC vendors are fully booked by April once the first warm week hits, and you don't want to be calling around the day your AC stops working in July. Most manufacturer warranties require documented annual service to stay valid.

entries.title: HVAC tune-up (heating)
entries.description: HVAC tech inspects and services the heating system before winter. Includes burner inspection and cleaning, heat exchanger check for cracks (carbon monoxide risk), gas valve and pilot test, blower motor service, thermostat calibration, and a full ignition cycle test. Critical safety check for gas-fired systems.
entries.notes: Book in August or early September. The first cold snap floods every HVAC vendor's voicemail and turns a routine $200 tune-up into a 2-week wait. Annual service is required to maintain most manufacturer warranties.

entries.title: Inspect ductwork for leaks
entries.description: HVAC tech runs a duct-leakage test (typically a Duct Blaster pressurization test or a manual smoke-pencil walkthrough) to find air loss in the supply and return ducts. Most homes lose 20–30% of conditioned air to duct leaks — sealing them recovers that money on every energy bill for the rest of the system's life.
entries.notes: Older homes (pre-2000) and homes with ductwork running through unconditioned spaces (attic, crawl) benefit most. If your second floor is always 5–10°F off the first floor, leaky ducts are the #1 suspect.

entries.title: Bleed radiators
entries.description: Boiler tech opens each radiator's bleed valve in turn to release trapped air, then tops off boiler pressure to spec. Trapped air at the top of a radiator means the bottom half can heat fine while the top stays cold — the room never gets warm even though the system runs constantly.
entries.notes: Most boiler owners include this in the annual boiler service visit instead of a separate appointment — no point paying two trip charges. If you've noticed any radiator running cold or only warming halfway, it's worth flagging to the tech.

entries.description: Plumber flushes a vinegar or commercial descaler solution through the tankless unit's heat exchanger for 30–45 minutes, then rinses with fresh water. entries.notes: Hard water areas (well water + most municipal water in the Northeast) may need every 6 months. If you notice the unit cycling more often or hot water taking longer to arrive, you're already overdue. Most manufacturer warranties require documented annual descaling.

entries.title: Top up turf infill
entries.description: Turf specialist refreshes the rubber or silica sand infill that holds the synthetic fibers upright. Infill migrates over time from rain runoff, foot traffic, and seasonal grooming. Without it, fibers mat down and the turf looks worn long before its 12–15 year design life.
entries.notes: Most synthetic-turf vendors offer this as part of an annual service plan. If you've noticed footprints staying visible after walking on the turf, you're already overdue.

entries.title: Power rake and groom turf
entries.description: Turf specialist runs a power rake or groomer across the surface to lift matted fibers, redistribute migrated infill, and remove debris that's worked into the pile. Keeps the turf looking new and bouncy through year 15+ instead of going flat at year 5.
entries.notes: Twice-a-year is the manufacturer recommendation for most premium turf. Spring grooming opens up the pile after winter compaction; fall grooming clears leaves and acorns before they break down into organic matter (which then feeds weed growth between blades).

entries.title: Deep clean synthetic turf
entries.description: Turf cleaning service uses a power groomer + extraction vacuum to pull embedded debris, pollen, dust, and pet residue out of the infill layer. Goes deeper than the annual top-up + grooming visit. Extends usable turf life by 3–5 years and resets the look to near-new for HNW homeowners who notice surface fade.
entries.notes: Schedule for early spring before the heaviest pollen weeks — that way the infill is clean before the year's accumulation starts. If you have dogs or kids using the turf heavily, consider every year rather than every two.

entries.description: Remove failing or stained grout from a defined section and re-grout. Sealing afterward extends the life of the new grout.

entries.description: Use the underside reset button and the manual hex key to free a jammed disposal. Quick fix when the disposal hums but won't spin.

entries.title: Replace kitchen faucet aerator
entries.description: Unscrew the kitchen aerator, descale or replace, and reinstall. Restores full flow on a faucet that's lost pressure.

entries.title: Clean range hood grease filters
entries.description: Remove the metal mesh filters and run them through the dishwasher or soak in degreaser. Restores hood efficiency and cuts fire risk.
entries.notes: Replace charcoal filters annually if your hood recirculates instead of vents outside.

entries.title: Replace refrigerator door gasket
entries.description: Swap a torn or compressed door seal so the fridge holds temperature. Compressor cycles less; ice and frost stop forming around the door.

entries.title: Tighten a loose kitchen sink
entries.description: Re-secure a sink that's pulled away from the countertop or shifted in the cutout. Stops water from running behind the cabinet.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Replace a worn dish soap or instant-hot pump
entries.title: Replace a worn dish soap or instant-hot pump
entries.description: Swap a dish soap dispenser pump or instant-hot dispenser that's leaking or no longer pumping. Bottle stays in place under the sink.

entries.title: Touch up exterior trim paint
entries.description: Spot-paint chips, peeling spots, and weather wear on door frames, window casings, and porch posts. Catches the next paint cycle before water damage starts.

entries.title: Replace damaged deck boards
entries.description: Swap warped, split, or rotted deck boards. The handyman matches species and stain so the patch blends with the rest of the deck.

entries.title: Repair or replace mailbox post
entries.description: Reset a leaning mailbox post or install a fresh one. Includes confirming the address numbers are visible from the street.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install house numbers or address plaque
entries.title: Install house numbers or address plaque
entries.description: Mount new address numbers or a plaque on the house, mailbox, or gate post. Improves visibility for emergency response and deliveries.

entries.title: Replace exterior light fixtures
entries.description: Swap a worn or dated porch, garage, or post light. Includes confirming the wiring is rated for the new fixture's wattage and the gasket seals against weather.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Patch concrete steps and small cracks
entries.title: Patch concrete steps and small cracks
entries.description: Fill chips, spalled corners, and surface cracks in concrete steps, walkways, or patios using a polymer-modified patch.

entries.title: Replace damaged fence pickets
entries.description: Swap rotted, broken, or warped fence pickets without replacing the whole run. Color-match stain so the repair blends.

entries.title: Spot re-stain a deck section
entries.description: Re-stain the highest-wear sections of a deck (rail tops, in front of doors, around the grill) without redoing the whole deck.

entries.title: Replace garage door bottom seal
entries.description: Swap the rubber threshold seal on the bottom of the garage door. Stops drafts, water, and pests from getting under the door.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Lubricate garage door rollers and hinges
entries.title: Lubricate garage door rollers and hinges
entries.description: Apply silicone or lithium-based lubricant to rollers, hinges, and the spring shaft. Quiets the door and extends opener and spring life.
entries.notes: Skip the springs unless you're a pro. High tension and risk of injury.

entries.title: Repair pull-down attic stairs
entries.description: Tighten or replace springs, replace a broken tread, or reset the latch on pull-down attic stairs. Restores safe access to attic storage.

entries.title: Patch chipped epoxy garage floor
entries.description: Spot-patch chipped or peeling epoxy in high-traffic areas of the garage. Re-coat the patch and feather into the surrounding finish.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install garage shelving or wall-mounted racks
entries.title: Install garage shelving or wall-mounted racks
entries.description: Mount garage shelving units, slatwall, ceiling-mounted overhead racks, or pegboard. Includes confirming wall studs / ceiling joists for safe load.

entries.title: Replace doorbell button (low-voltage)
entries.description: Swap a worn or dated doorbell button at the front door. Easy fix when the button no longer rings consistently.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Install smart smoke and CO detectors
entries.title: Install smart smoke and CO detectors
entries.description: Replace older battery detectors with hardwired or interconnected smart detectors (Nest, First Alert) and confirm the network reports correctly.

entries.title: Replace thermostat batteries
entries.description: Swap the AA or AAA backup batteries in a battery-powered or hybrid-power thermostat. Prevents the mid-cold-snap thermostat blackout.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Place or relocate smart leak sensors
entries.title: Place or relocate smart leak sensors
entries.description: Move existing smart leak sensors to higher-risk spots (under sinks, behind washing machine, near water heater) or add a new round of placements.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Mount and configure a smart camera
entries.title: Mount and configure a smart camera
entries.description: Install a battery- or wired smart camera, secure to the mount, and configure motion zones in the app.

entries.templateKey: Handyman:Mount a TV on the wall
entries.title: Mount a TV on the wall
entries.description: Install a wall-mount TV bracket, secure to studs, hang the TV, and route the cables. Includes confirming the bracket is rated for the TV weight.

entries.title: Install floating shelves
entries.description: Hang floating shelves with concealed brackets. Includes confirming the wall stud or anchor type matches the load rating of the shelf.

entries.title: Hang a gallery wall (3+ frames)
entries.description: Lay out, level, and hang a multi-frame arrangement. Includes a paper template pass so you see the layout before any holes go in the wall.

entries.title: Assemble flat-pack furniture
entries.description: Assemble desk, dresser, bookcase, or other knock-down furniture. Includes leveling and confirming all hardware is fully torqued.

entries.title: Install a closet organizer system
entries.description: Install a wire, melamine, or wood closet system. Includes layout planning, anchor placement, and final shelf and rod adjustment.

entries.title: Mount curtain rods and hardware
entries.description: Install curtain or drapery rods, hold-backs, and finials. Includes confirming the bracket is anchored to a stud or rated drywall anchor.

entries.title: Renew snow plowing contract
entries.description: Most snow plow vendors require a signed seasonal contract by mid-fall. Reach out to confirm pricing, set the trigger snowfall depth, and authorize per-storm billing for the season ahead.
entries.notes: Contract typically covers Nov 1 – Apr 1 in the Northeast. Lock it in before October.

entries.templateKey: Mosquito & Tick:Sign up for mosquito and tick season
entries.title: Sign up for mosquito and tick season
entries.description: Most mosquito and tick vendors run seasonal programs — an every-3-week spray schedule from April through October. Sign up in early spring to lock in your spot on their schedule.
entries.notes: Some vendors offer all-natural cedar-oil alternatives if you prefer. Talk to your vendor about program start date so you're covered before tick season peaks.

entries.title: Annual tree assessment
entries.description: Certified arborist walks the property identifying dead limbs, structural weakness, disease, and storm risk. A $300 annual visit catches the $30,000 problems.
entries.notes: Best done in early spring before leaf-out so the structural picture is clear.

entries.title: Pruning and crown thinning
entries.description: Selective pruning of mature trees to reduce wind load, eliminate hazardous limbs, and maintain structure. Should be done by an ISA-certified arborist, not a landscaper.
entries.notes: Dormant-season pruning (Dec-Mar) is safest for the trees and cheapest for you.

entries.templateKey: Tree Service:Trim trees away from roof
entries.title: Trim trees away from roof
entries.description: Arborist trims back branches within 10 feet of the roof to prevent storm damage and reduce moss buildup.
entries.notes: Arborist required for large trees

entries.title: Exterior window washing
entries.description: Professional washing of all exterior windows, screens, frame tracks, and sills using purified water systems that leave a streak-free finish without chemical residue. Includes a wipe-down of the frames and removal of any caked pollen, spider webs, and bird debris that builds up in upper corners.
entries.notes: Spring after pollen settles and fall before storm windows go on. Quarterly for homes that need to stay immaculate (waterfront, heavy shade with sap, or homes with frequent entertaining). Most premium services include sill and screen cleaning at no extra charge.

entries.title: Annual exterior power washing
entries.description: Soft-wash crew applies a low-pressure cleaning solution and rinses the siding, deck, walkways, and patio. Removes mildew, pollen, and dirt buildup that accumulates over the year and restores curb appeal in one visit. The 'soft-wash' approach (chemistry-driven, low pressure) avoids the wood damage and oxidation streaking that high-pressure washing can cause on siding and decks.
entries.notes: Schedule for late spring after the heaviest pollen settles — that way the cleaning lasts the longest into summer. Hardscape (concrete, stone, pavers) is more forgiving and can take higher pressure if needed. Always confirm with the vendor that they're using soft-wash on siding before they start.

entries.title: Asphalt driveway sealcoat
entries.description: Apply fresh sealcoat to the driveway. Protects against water infiltration, UV damage, and fuel spills.
entries.notes: Apply in early fall while temps are still warm enough for the sealer to cure properly.

entries.title: Annual attic inspection
entries.description: Handyman or attic specialist visually inspects for insulation displacement, pest entry signs, roof-underside leaks, and ventilation issues.
entries.notes: Often included in a fall handyman visit.

entries.title: Annual elevator inspection
entries.description: Certified elevator inspector verifies code compliance: emergency stop, door sensors and interlocks, governor and safety brake, hoist cable wear, machine room ventilation, and updated certificate posting. Required by state law in most jurisdictions for residential elevators — failing to keep current can void homeowner's insurance for elevator-related claims.
entries.notes: Keep the certificate on file with other estate documents. If your home is on a service contract with an elevator company (Otis, ThyssenKrupp, etc.), the inspection is usually included — but the certificate is something you need to pull and file yourself.

entries.title: Quarterly elevator service
entries.description: Routine service visit covering cable tension and inspection, rail and roller lubrication, door sensor calibration, emergency phone test, and cab leveling check. Catches wear before a small issue becomes a stuck-between-floors call.
entries.notes: Most homes are on a quarterly service contract with the installer or a local specialist. If you've never used the emergency phone, this visit is when to test it — phone batteries die silently and you don't want to find out you can't call out from inside the cab during the next power blip.

entries.title: Annual cooling unit service
entries.description: Wine cellar specialist services the dedicated cooling unit: cleans evaporator and condenser coils (a clogged coil silently raises cellar temp by 5–10°F), checks refrigerant charge against spec, verifies thermostat calibration to within 1°F, tests humidity controls (ideal: 60–70% RH), and inspects the drain line for the condensate.
entries.notes: Cooling unit failures can ruin a collection overnight — fine wine starts heat-damaging at 75°F+, and most modern units have no built-in alarm if the compressor fails on a Friday night. This is not a category to skip. Most manufacturer warranties require annual documented service.

entries.title: Annual radon test
entries.description: Place a short-term radon detector kit in the lowest livable level for 2-7 days, then mail it to the lab. Levels above 4 pCi/L require mitigation; 2-4 pCi/L is borderline and worth re-testing. A handyman can handle placement and collection; you don't need a certified radon tester unless you need a real-estate-transaction report.
entries.notes: NH, CT, and much of the surrounding Northeast are in the granite belt, one of the highest radon zones in the country.

entries.templateKey: Air Quality:Service whole-home or basement dehumidifier
entries.title: Service whole-home or basement dehumidifier
entries.description: Clean the filter, wipe the coils, check the drain line for clogs, and verify the humidistat calibration. Catches silent failures that let basements creep above 60% RH and invite mold.
entries.notes: Pair with the spring handyman visit; run a humidity reading after service to confirm.
